title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data egress failure inside a developer tool, not a model error. The upload happened in the default configuration of the coding assistant, at the point where the Codebase Indexing feature read a local repository. Nothing in the reporting shows a user action that triggered it, which places the failure in the shipped defaults rather than in how developers used the product.

Catching it would have required the indexing feature to be off until a user turned it on, or a clear prompt before any repository content left the machine. A review of what the default settings transmit, and to where, would have surfaced the upload path before release. The patch and the later disabling of that path came after developers reported it.

What is not established is whether any code data was retained, since the finding of no retention comes from Z.ai's own reviews rather than an outside determination. The claim that six workspaces with sensitive data were uploaded was retracted by the company that made it, so it is not a finding. Intent is not established by the reporting.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Developers reported that Z.ai's ZCode AI coding assistant uploaded local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without consent. Z.ai said a default-enabled Codebase Indexing feature caused this, apologized, patched the vulnerability, and later disabled the upload path. One company retracted a separate claim that six workspaces containing sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai said independent reviews found no code data retained.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
